# Third-party notices

`Sources/AU05Device/Protocol.swift` adapts report encryption/decryption, command formats and physical button identifiers from [AU05 Keys](https://github.com/elliclee/ulanzi-au05-keys), revision `7819351a5ba5c68874d0519fabe3bf62db47e328` (`Battery.swift`, `VendorKeys.swift`, `Core.swift`). Copyright (c) 2026 AU05 Keys contributors. The complete MIT license is retained in [AU05-Keys-LICENSE](AU05-Keys-LICENSE) and included in app bundles.

The native HID transport and lifecycle are implemented here. No Ulanzi proprietary binary or firmware is distributed.

The optional DualSense microphone helper bundles libopus from [Opus / Xiph.Org](https://opus-codec.org/). Its upstream [copyright and license notices](Opus-COPYING.txt) are retained here and shipped in the app resources as `Opus-COPYING.txt`. These third-party notices remain independent of the VibeWand noncommercial license.

Command mode's kernel is assembled by `scripts/build-kernel.sh` and shipped in the app under `Contents/Resources/kernel`; none of it is stored in this repository.

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 24.21.0, the official Apple Silicon build, unmodified and with its original signature. Its license, which also covers the libraries built into it, ships as `kernel/node/LICENSE`.
- [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 0.2.0-rc.2 (MIT), limited to the packages VibeWand's coordinator bundle names (`kernel/coordinator/package.json`), the launcher's own support packages and, since 0.10.0, its SenseVoice plug-in (`kernel/package.json`), together with the dependencies recorded in `kernel/package-lock.json`. Among those is its multi-provider model component, which builds on [pi-ai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-ai) (MIT) and on the SDKs of the services it can reach: OpenAI (Apache-2.0), Anthropic (MIT), Google Gen AI (Apache-2.0) and AWS (Apache-2.0).
- Installed on Apple Silicon, the kernel holds 222 packages besides VibeWand's own bundle. 79 are DeepSeek Harness's own, MIT apart from two under BSD-3-Clause. The other 143 come from third parties, under the MIT (83), Apache-2.0 (40), BSD-3-Clause (12), ISC (4), 0BSD, Python-2.0, Unlicense and LGPL-3.0-or-later (one each) licenses. Each names its license in its own `package.json` inside `kernel/node_modules`, and all but twelve also carry the license text there: nine MIT or Apache-2.0 packages published without a license file of their own, the two sherpa-onnx packages and the prebuilt libvips, both described next. An earlier wording of this notice gave 216 as the number of third-party packages; that figure counted the harness's own packages too.
- Dictation's SenseVoice service runs the recogniser of the harness's SenseVoice plug-in (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-speech-to-text-sensevoice`, MIT). The plug-in uses [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) 1.13.8 (Apache-2.0): the package `sherpa-onnx-node` and the prebuilt `sherpa-onnx-darwin-arm64`, shipped unmodified under `kernel/node_modules`, about 34 MB, and loaded only while SenseVoice recognises a recording. Neither package carries a license text, so the texts are kept here and shipped in the app resources: sherpa-onnx's license as [sherpa-onnx-LICENSE](sherpa-onnx-LICENSE), and for the prebuilt package's `libonnxruntime.dylib`, which is [ONNX Runtime](https://onnxruntime.ai) 1.28.2 (MIT, Microsoft Corporation), its license as [ONNX-Runtime-LICENSE](ONNX-Runtime-LICENSE) with the notices for the libraries built into it as [ONNX-Runtime-ThirdPartyNotices.txt](ONNX-Runtime-ThirdPartyNotices.txt). The three are the files of those versions as their projects publish them. This is new in 0.10.0.
- The prebuilt package's `libsherpa-onnx-c-api.dylib` has more than sherpa-onnx built into it. sherpa-onnx's build files for 1.13.8 (the `cmake` folder of its repository) name the libraries and the revisions used, and the file that ships holds code of each: kaldi-native-fbank, kaldi-decoder, kaldifst, OpenFst and simple-sentencepiece (Apache-2.0, the license in `sherpa-onnx-LICENSE`), JSON for Modern C++ and piper-phonemize (MIT), hclust-cpp (BSD-2-Clause), Eigen (MPL-2.0, source at [libeigen/eigen](https://gitlab.com/libeigen/eigen)) and, for speech synthesis, [eSpeak NG](https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng) in the fork `csukuangfj/espeak-ng`, under **GPL-3.0-or-later**. VibeWand only recognises speech and never calls the synthesis code, but that code is in the library as published, and 0.10.0 ships the library as it is. **Not in this folder yet:** the GNU GPL 3.0 text and a pointer to eSpeak NG's source, and the MIT and BSD notices of JSON for Modern C++, piper-phonemize and hclust-cpp. The way out that is preferred, taking this one library from the build sherpa-onnx publishes without speech synthesis, has not been tried.
- The models SenseVoice needs are not part of the app and are not stored in this repository. When the user asks for them, VibeWand downloads the files the plug-in pins from Hugging Face or its mirror: SenseVoiceSmall as converted for sherpa-onnx (`csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-sense-voice-zh-en-ja-ko-yue-2024-07-17`, from [FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice](https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice)) and Silero VAD (`csukuangfj/vad`, from [snakers4/silero-vad](https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad), MIT). The original model, [FunAudioLLM/SenseVoiceSmall](https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/SenseVoiceSmall), is published by Alibaba Group under the [FunASR Model Open Source License Agreement 1.1](https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR/blob/main/MODEL_LICENSE), which asks whoever uses or shares it to name the source and author and to keep the model's name.
- The harness's picture store (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local`), which holds a picture a tool shows the model, uses [sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com) 0.35.5 (Apache-2.0) and with it the prebuilt [libvips](https://www.libvips.org) for Apple Silicon, `@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64` 1.3.4, under **LGPL-3.0-or-later**. It is one dynamic library, `kernel/node_modules/@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64/lib/libvips-cpp.8.18.7.dylib`, shipped unmodified, loaded only when the model is shown a picture, and replaceable with a build of your own. The `README.md` beside it lists every library built into it with its license (among them glib, pango, librsvg, libheif, libexif and fribidi under the LGPL, cairo under the MPL 1.1), `versions.json` gives their versions, and the build recipes with pointers to the sources are at [lovell/sharp-libvips](https://github.com/lovell/sharp-libvips). This is new in 0.10.0. **Not in this folder yet:** the texts of the GNU LGPL 3.0 and GPL 3.0; the package itself carries neither.

**Open items.** What is marked “not in this folder yet” above, the license texts of nine packages published without one, the terms of the SenseVoice models and the other licensing questions still open are listed, with the ways to settle each, in [`docs/licensing-open-items.md`](../docs/licensing-open-items.md) of the repository. The owner decided on 2026-10-06 to settle them before the project is opened; 0.10.0 is published in the private repository with them open.

VibeWand's coordinator bundle (`kernel/coordinator`, installed in the kernel as the package `vibewand-coordinator`) is part of VibeWand. The same bundle, and the overlay beside it (`kernel/overlay`), ship as `Contents/Resources/harness/` for a DeepSeek Harness the user installed themselves. In that mode nothing of the harness is shipped or modified: the user's own installation runs it.
